value.body: The Indian Statistical Service is a Group A central service for statisticians, recruited through UPSC's combined Indian Economic Service / Indian Statistical Service examination. ISS officers work on official statistics — surveys, national accounts, price indices and data systems — mainly under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation and in statistics units of other ministries.

items.label: Exam
items.note: Held once a year; written papers followed by a personality test

items.label: Marks
items.note: General English and General Studies (100 each) plus four Statistics papers (200 each)

items.label: Age limit
items.note: Relaxation for SC/ST, OBC and PwBD as per rules

items.label: ISS posts notified
items.note: UPSC notes the number can change

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree with Statistics, Mathematical Statistics or Applied Statistics as one of the subjects, or a master's degree in one of these. You apply to the UPSC IES/ISS notification (usually released in February), clear the written exam and then the interview.

value.title: At a glance
items: Very few posts each year, so competition is intense.
Two Statistics papers are objective and two are descriptive, covering probability, inference, sampling, econometrics, demography and more.
Selected officers go through induction training and then postings in official statistics work across the country.

value.title: ISS posts notified by UPSC
value.note: Approximate numbers from each year's notice; final vacancies can differ (2024's final result listed 33 including backlog).
